transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (HaloHealth CTO), Samir Khan (HaloHealth Head of Data), Priya Mehta (HaloHealth Security Lead)

Summary: Quick POC scoping to align on data handling requirements — PII, logging/redaction, retention, prompt storage, benchmarks and timelines. Agreed to a 3-week POC with benchmark targets and a security questionnaire follow-up.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Lena here, CTO at HaloHealth, short on time today but really want to make sure we nail data handling for the POC.
[00:15] Maya Patel: Perfect. Jordan, want to do a quick intro from SE side?
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Yep, Jordan Lee, Redwood SE, I focus on inference perf and privacy controls. We'll run the benchmarks and help wire up your data paths.
[00:25] Samir Khan: Samir, head of data. We'll be providing sample de-identified and synthetic datasets for the POC, and also want to test with a small subset of real records under strict controls.
[00:35] Priya Mehta: Priya, I cover security and compliance; our key ask is how PII is handled, what logs are kept, how prompts are stored, retention settings, and encryption/KMS options.
[00:46] Maya Patel: Great. Goal today is to scope the POC: success criteria, workload size, benchmark targets, timeline, and data handling specifics.
[00:54] Jordan Lee: To add — we'll propose a 3-week POC: week 1 integration and dataset onboarding, week 2 run benchmarks and iterate, week 3 analyze results and wrap up. Does that align?
[01:05] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Sounds reasonable. Success criteria for us — latencies under 200ms p50 for the chat path, throughput to handle 50 concurrent users during peak, and zero PII persisted in logs. Also we want reproducible benchmarks vs our current self-hosted stack.
[01:22] Maya Patel: Noted. Jordan, on the PII and logs — what are Redwood's options for redaction and retention during a POC?
[01:30] Jordan Lee: We support configurable retention windows at the tenant level; for POCs we can set retention to zero days or disable transcript retention entirely. We also have automatic PII redaction — it's a best-effort NLP-based filter, so for PHI we usually recommend pre-redaction on your side plus our runtime redaction as a safety net.
[01:49] Priya Mehta: When you say "disable retention" — does that mean no prompts or responses are stored anywhere in your hosted logs?
[01:57] Jordan Lee: Correct, for the POC we can set retention to 0 and exclude prompt text from analytics. There will still be operational metadata (latency, token counts, request IDs) for debugging unless you opt out of those.
[02:08] Samir Khan: We need to make sure the prompt storage is also controllable — we do not want raw user prompts persisted due to HIPAA concerns.
[02:15] Jordan Lee: Understood. Options: 1) Do not send PII in prompts — do client-side redaction; 2) Use token-level masking on our SDK which strips fields before sending; 3) Use Redwood Private (VPC) where logs remain in your VPC and you control S3 buckets/retention. For this POC we can do (2) plus retention=0 to satisfy HaloHealth requirements.
[02:36] Dr. Lena Ortiz: How well does the redaction handle clinical abbreviations? e.g., "MI" could be myocardial infarction or something else.
[02:44] Jordan Lee: Good point — automated redaction can mislabel abbreviations. We'll include a small prompt-level redaction test in the benchmark to measure false negatives/positives. We'll also supply the redaction config so you can add domain-specific patterns.
[02:57] Priya Mehta: We also require that all keys are customer-managed KMS; can Redwood support envelope encryption with our key?
[03:05] Jordan Lee: For Private deployments yes, you're in control. For hosted POC we can integrate with your cloud KMS for certain artifacts; full BYOK for all logs is a Private feature. For hosted, we can arrange limited KMS integration for model artifacts and storage with an agreement.
[03:21] Maya Patel: To be explicit: for the POC we propose hosted with retention disabled + SDK-based field stripping + audit logs sent to your SIEM via webhook, or if you're more comfortable we can do a short Private eval. Which do you prefer?
[03:34] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Prefer hosted if we can get the assurances: no prompt retention, KMS integration for artifacts, and a clear audit trail export.
[03:42] Samir Khan: Also need to test performance with our in-house pre-processing pipeline. Our estimated workload for the POC: 10k requests/day, average 120 tokens per request, peaks up to 50 concurrent.
[03:55] Jordan Lee: That's helpful. For sizing, that maps to roughly a single dedicated slice on our Dedicated product, but for POC the hosted pool will handle it — we'll simulate peak concurrency during benchmarks. Our benchmark harness will run synthetic concurrency with your token distribution.
[04:12] Priya Mehta: About logging — you said operational metadata remains. Can we route those metrics directly to our Datadog without storing them in Redwood long-term?
[04:20] Jordan Lee: Yes — we can stream metrics to Datadog/Prometheus; retention in Redwood is independent. For POC we can disable internal retention and forward metrics to your observability account.
[04:31] Dr. Lena Ortiz: What about inference outputs — are they ever used to improve Redwood models or for training? We need guarantees for data usage.
[04:39] Jordan Lee: Redwood's policy for customer data: hosted POC data is not used to train public models; for enterprise we have contractual clauses that prohibit data usage. We'll share the data processing addendum. For the POC we'll explicitly set the flag to opt-out of any training or telemetry ingestion beyond debug metrics.
[04:55] Samir Khan: Good. On benchmarks — we want to compare p50/p95 latencies and token cost per request vs our current baseline. Can you provide a spreadsheet template?
[05:03] Jordan Lee: Yep, I'll share the benchmark spreadsheet and a harness (script) you can run against our endpoint. We'll populate initial runs and then run a 24-hour soak with your payload distribution.
[05:14] Maya Patel: Success criteria recap: p50 <200ms, p95 <600ms, support 50 concurrent users at peak without timeouts, zero persisted PII, retention=0 for prompts, KMS for artifacts if possible, mocked patient data for accuracy tests.
[05:30] Dr. Lena Ortiz: We also want to measure quality regression — ensure answers meet clinical QA thresholds. We'll provide a small eval set of 200 items.
[05:38] Jordan Lee: We'll run QA evals and attach pass/fail metrics to the benchmark CSV. We'll also snapshot model versions so results are reproducible.
[05:47] Priya Mehta: One more security note — we need SAML SSO and RBAC for console access, and audit logs for any user that views the raw prompt (if at all).
[05:58] Jordan Lee: SAML SSO and RBAC are standard for enterprise. For the POC we can set up temporary RBAC roles and make sure only AE/SE + your named engineers have console access. Any access to raw prompts will be disabled for your tenant.
[06:12] Samir Khan: Timeline check — if you send the POC proposal by Friday (2026-03-06) we can sign and start integration on 2026-03-16. That fits our release cycle.
[06:21] Maya Patel: That's the plan. We'll include two bench scenarios: synthetic concurrency run and a 24-hour soak with sampled payloads. We'll also include the redaction tests and the eval set run.
[06:34] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Pricing will matter — do you have an estimate for the hosted POC cost?
[06:39] Maya Patel: We'll put a POC rate in the proposal — usually a fixed fee covering compute and engineering support. Jordan, do you want to ballpark?
[06:46] Jordan Lee: Ballpark for the described load and 3-week engagement with engineering support is in the low tens of thousands, but we'll firm that up in the proposal.
[06:55] Priya Mehta: Please include the security docs: SOC 2 Type II report, encryption whitepaper, data processing addendum.
[07:02] Maya Patel: We'll attach those with the proposal.
[07:06] Samir Khan: Anything else?
[07:08] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Also, please mark anything that requires Private deployment (BYOK, no-hosted logs) vs hosted options. We want to evaluate both from a risk perspective.
[07:18] Jordan Lee: Will do — proposal will have two tracks: hosted POC with retention disabled and SDK redaction, or short Private eval with BYOK and no external storage.
[07:27] Maya Patel: OK recap of next steps: Maya send proposal+pricing (by 3/6), Jordan send benchmark harness & spreadsheet (by 3/5), Priya send completed security questionnaire (by 3/7), schedule kickoff week of 3/16.
[07:40] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Good. Thanks all.
[07:43] Maya Patel: Thanks, we'll follow up in email and attach the docs.
[07:46] (call ends)
